guard: The mesh handler's turn client is real: the submission rides the run roster and carries the rendered context, the bound external is what a resume re-enters, the client's own pause is the L4003 authority and its presence watch the L4002 authority, a deny's turn-deadline reason maps to L4003, notices are consumed by the carrying goal, and handoff honoring (memo spend, L4005/L4004 validation, the handoffFrom link, adoption seeding) actually happens, and the agent's permits are metered at the turn (turns spent per dispatch and read back from the journal at adoption, wall clock against the turn's deadline, unmeterable budgets refused at spawn)
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/mesh-turn.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: Lane F durable-actions step 6 (2026-09-02): `turn` leaves the not-yet-durable seam and
performs through the manager's pull-shaped relay. The client half lives in mesh-handler.ts,
which the suite imports through a relative `../src` path — no build sits between the mutation
and the run. Each obligation has a mutant: the roster the submission rides (TM9), the bound
external a resume re-enters (TM12), the client's own deadline authority (TM8) and the deny's
reason mapping (TM7), the presence watch that is the run's sole L4002 authority under the
executor-currency rule (TM6), the pause claimed on a terminal (TM10), notice consumption by
the carrying goal (TM5), and the handoff machinery: the memo riding the submission (TM1),
its immediate-only spend (TM2), the L4005/L4004 yield validation (TM3/TM4), the
adoption-time seeding (TM11), the marked seat death on a deny (L4002, not L4003) and the acceptance's own deadline instant.
Batch B1 (2026-09-03) adds the permits meter: the turns gate, the wall-clock gate, the
per-dispatch spend, the adoption-time count from recorded turn entries, and the refusal of
a budget this host has no meter for.

Batch B2 (2026-09-03) folds the adopted append log to the journal's keyed view before seeding: one record per step, so a turn is charged once, a failed spawn holds no worktree, and a cancelled turn is not re-registered.
Batch B2 (2026-09-03): the permit is spent by a turn that BOUND (the same event the
adoption seed counts), and one classifier reads a refused acceptance on both submits.
